## Why This Is Asked
Tests partitioned StatefulSet upgrades, PDB, and probes in a real CKAD scenario.

## Key Concepts
- StatefulSet partitioned RollingUpdate
- PodDisruptionBudget for minimum availability
- readinessProbe and startupProbe usage
- Resource requests/limits in containers

## Code Example
```javascript
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: StatefulSet
metadata:
  name: cache
  namespace: prod
spec:
  serviceName: "cache"
  replicas: 3
  updateStrategy:
    type: RollingUpdate
    rollingUpdate:
      partition: 2
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: cache
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: cache
        image: myrepo/cache:2.0
        resources:
          requests:
            cpu: "100m"
            memory: "128Mi"
          limits:
            cpu: "300m"
            memory: "256Mi"
        readinessProbe:
          exec:
            command: ["bash","-lc","redis-cli PING"]
          initialDelaySeconds: 5
          periodSeconds: 10
        startupProbe:
          exec:
            command: ["bash","-lc","true"]
          initialDelaySeconds: 10
          periodSeconds: 30
```

```javascript
apiVersion: policy/v1
kind: PodDisruptionBudget
metadata:
  name: cache-pdb
  namespace: prod
spec:
  minAvailable: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: cache
```

## Diagram
flowchart TD
  A[Partitioned Upgrade] --> B[Staged Pods Updated]

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you revert if the upgrade fails?
- How would you monitor for anomalies during the upgrade?

Assesses practical CKAD mastery of production-ready deployments, autoscaling configuration, and operational safety measures in Kubernetes environments.

- Resource requests/limits for predictable performance and resource allocation
- Readiness and liveness probes for health monitoring and traffic management
- HorizontalPodAutoscaler for dynamic scaling based on CPU utilization
- PodDisruptionBudget for availability guarantees during maintenance
- RollingUpdate strategy for controlled deployments with zero downtime

```yaml
  requests:
    cpu: "100m"
    memory: "128Mi"

readinessProbe:
```

```yaml
kind: HorizontalPodAutoscaler
```

## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to design a namespace-scoped DNS audit using only Kubernetes primitives: ConfigMaps/Secrets, InitContainers, a small main container, and a network policy.

## Key Concepts
- Namespace-scoped Deployment and ConfigMap usage
- InitContainer to install tooling (bind-tools)
- Lightweight agent script to enumerate Services and perform dig checks
- External POST of results with secrets
- TLS sidecar for rotation and NetworkPolicy for egress control

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: dns-audit
  namespace: example
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: dns-audit
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: dns-audit
    spec:
      initContainers:
        - name: installer
          image: alpine:3.18
          command: ["sh", "-c", "apk add --no-cache bind-tools curl"]
      containers:
        - name: auditor
          image: myorg/dns-audit:latest
          # script runs periodically via sleep loop
          env:
            - name: DNS_ALLOWLIST_CONFIGMAP
              value: dns-config
```

- How would you handle rate limits if namespace scale grows?
- How to test this in a local cluster without external endpoints?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests CKAD ability to compose a small, namespace-scoped verification workflow that touches ConfigMaps, Secrets, PVCs, and network policy.

## Key Concepts
- Deployment with InitContainer
- ConfigMap-based allowlist
- Secret-based credentials and TLS sidecar
- PVC-mounted /secrets and lightweight parsing with jq/yq
- Readiness/Liveness probes and per-namespace NetworkPolicy

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: compliance-api-creds
  namespace: default
data:
  token: <base64>
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: secret-allowlist
  namespace: default
data:
  allowed_keys: |
    tls.key
    tls.crt
    creds
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: secret-compliance-checker
  namespace: default
spec:
  replicas: 1
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: secret-compliance-checker
    spec:
      initContainers:
        - name: install-tools
          image: alpine:3.18
          command: ["sh", "-c", "apk add --no-cache jq curl && wget -O - https://github.com/yq-dev/yq/releases/latest/download/yq_linux_amd64 -O /usr/local/bin/yq && chmod +x /usr/local/bin/yq"]
      containers:
        - name: checker
          image: alpine:3.18
          command: ["/bin/sh", "-c", "./check.sh"]
          volumeMounts:
            - name: secrets
              mountPath: /secrets
      volumes:
        - name: secrets
          persistentVolumeClaim:
            claimName: secret-storage
      readinessProbe:
        httpGet:
          path: /healthz
          port: 8080
        initialDelaySeconds: 5
        periodSeconds: 10
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you scale and test this in a real cluster?
- What are risks with mounting Secrets in /secrets and how to mitigate?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests practical use of ConfigMaps, envFrom, and volume mounting; checks how changes trigger controlled rollouts with an annotation-based restart cue; covers health checks basics.

## Key Concepts
- Deployments, ConfigMaps, envFrom
- Volumes and ConfigMap mounts
- Rolling restarts via PodTemplate annotations
- Readiness and Liveness probes
- Trade-offs: restart cost vs. up-to-date config, ConfigMap size impacts, security

## Code Example
```yaml
# ConfigMap skeleton
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: feature-flags
data:
  FLAG_A: "true"
  FLAG_B: "false"
---
# Deployment skeleton
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: feature-flag-service
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: feature-flag-service
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: feature-flag-service
      annotations:
        checksum.feature-flags: "{{ .Values.configMap.checksum }}"
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: nginx:alpine
        envFrom:
        - configMapRef:
            name: feature-flags
        volumeMounts:
        - name: config-volume
          mountPath: /config/flags
        readinessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /healthz
            port: 80
          initialDelaySeconds: 5
        livenessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /healthz
            port: 80
          initialDelaySeconds: 10
      volumes:
      - name: config-volume
        configMap:
          name: feature-flags
```

## Trade-offs Discussion
- **Restart Cost vs. Fresh Config**: Rolling restarts ensure configuration consistency but cause temporary availability reduction
- **ConfigMap Size Impact**: Large ConfigMaps increase annotation length and may affect API server performance
- **Security Considerations**: Environment variables expose config to process inspection; file mounts provide better isolation
- **Update Latency**: Annotation-based restarts are immediate but may be disruptive compared to hot-reload approaches

## Why This Is Asked
Tests practical Kubernetes hardening: securityContext at both pod and container levels, probes that reflect real app health, and a deterministic rolling update trigger. It also checks how to verify and rollback in a live system.

## Key Concepts
- PodSecurityContext and Container SecurityContext
- Probes: readiness vs liveness
- Rolling updates via PodTemplate changes (image digest annotation)
- Verification and rollback workflows

## Code Example
```yaml
# Patch sketch (showing key fields)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: worker
spec:
  template:
    metadata:
      annotations:
        kubernetes.io/change-cause: 'security-hardening'
    spec:
      securityContext:
        runAsNonRoot: true
        runAsUser: 1000
      containers:
      - name: worker
        image: your/image:tag
        securityContext:
          readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
          allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
          capabilities:
            drop: ["ALL"]
        readinessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /healthz
            port: 80
        livenessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /readyz
            port: 80
```

```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: DaemonSet
metadata:
  name: log-collector
spec:
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: log-collector

      labels:
        app: log-collector

        kubernetes.io/os: linux

            cpu: "500m"
            memory: "256Mi"
``` 

## Why This Is Asked
Tests RBAC scoping, CronJob scheduling, and in-cluster data backup to a ConfigMap without leaking secrets.

## Key Concepts
- RBAC granularity scoped to a namespace
- CronJob scheduling and Job templates
- Reading Kubernetes events via API in-cluster
- Updating/creating a ConfigMap from a Job

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ServiceAccount
metadata:
  name: events-backup-sa
  namespace: metrics
---
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: Role
metadata:
  name: events-backup-role
  namespace: metrics
rules:
- apiGroups: [""]
  resources: ["events"]
  verbs: ["get","list","watch"]
- apiGroups: [""]
  resources: ["configmaps"]
  verbs: ["get","update","create","patch"]
---
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: RoleBinding
metadata:
  name: events-backup-binding
  namespace: metrics
roleRef:
  apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io
  kind: Role
  name: events-backup-role
subjects:
- kind: ServiceAccount
  name: events-backup-sa
  namespace: metrics
---
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: events-backup
  namespace: metrics
spec:
  schedule: "*/2 * * * *"
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      template:
        spec:
          serviceAccountName: events-backup-sa
          containers:
          - name: backup
            image: bitnami/kubectl:latest
            command: ["/bin/sh","-c","kubectl get events -n metrics -o json | jq '.items[0:50]' > /backup/events.json; kubectl create configmap events-backup --from-file=events.json=/backup/events.json -n metrics --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -"]
          restartPolicy: OnFailure
          volumes:
          - name: backup
            emptyDir: {}
```

## Why This Is Asked

## Code Example
```yaml
# Minimal skeleton
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: feature-proxy
  namespace: ckad-demo
spec:
  replicas: 1
  template:
    spec:
      initContainers:
        - name: render-nginx
          image: alpine:3.18
          command: ["sh", "-c", "jq ... && render-nginx-conf.sh"]
      containers:
        - name: nginx
          image: nginx:alpine
          ports:
            - containerPort: 80
          volumeMounts:
            - name: config
              mountPath: /etc/nginx/nginx.conf
              subPath: nginx.conf
      volumes:
        - name: config
          emptyDir: {}
```

## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to compose CKAD primitives into a namespace-scoped automation task; exercises ConfigMaps, Secrets, PVCs, InitContainers, CronJob, NetworkPolicy, Sidecar, and RBAC.

## Key Concepts
- CronJob per-namespace
- ConfigMap/Secret usage
- InitContainer to install tooling
- Volume mounts with PVC
- HTTP POST from container
- Sidecar TLS rotation
- NetworkPolicy egress control
- Probes readiness/liveness
- Minimal YAML skeleton

## Code Example
```yaml
# Minimal CronJob skeleton (per-namespace)
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: template-renderer
spec:
  schedule: "*/60 * * * *"
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      template:
        spec:
          volumes:
          - name: templates
            persistentVolumeClaim:
              claimName: templates-pvc
          - name: artifacts
            persistentVolumeClaim:
              claimName: artifacts-pvc
          initContainers:
          - name: install-tools
            image: alpine:3.18
            command: ["sh", "-c", "apk add --no-cache gettext-base bash curl jq;"]
          containers:
          - name: render
            image: alpine:3.18
            command: ["sh", "-c", "render.sh"]
            volumeMounts:
            - name: templates
              mountPath: /templates
            - name: artifacts
              mountPath: /artifacts
          restartPolicy: OnFailure
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you test retries and backoff for the POST?
- How would you rotate credentials without pod restarts?

## Why This Is Asked
Tests end-to-end CKAD skills: per-namespace scoping, InitContainers, in-cluster secret handling, result storage via ConfigMap/Secret, and network policies. Encourages concrete YAML design rather than abstract concepts.

## Key Concepts
- InitContainers for tool setup
- In-namespace Secret/ConfigMap usage
- In-cluster traffic control with NetworkPolicy
- Sidecar for TLS cert rotation
- Post/aggregate results in-cluster

## Code Example
```yaml
# Minimal skeleton (Deployment, Secret, ConfigMap placeholders)
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: registry-creds
type: Opaque
data:
  username: <base64>
  password: <base64>
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: image-scan-config
data:
  registry: my-registry.io
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: image-scan
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: image-scan
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: image-scan
    spec:
      initContainers:
      - name: installer
        image: alpine:3.18
        command: ["sh", "-c", "apk add --no-cache trivy; mkdir -p /tools"]
        volumeMounts:
        - name: images
          mountPath: /images
      containers:
      - name: scanner
        image: alpine:3.18
        command: ["sh", "-c", "while read img; do trivy image $img --format json >> /reports/scan.json; done < /images/list.txt"]
        volumeMounts:
        - name: images
          mountPath: /images
      volumes:
      - name: images
        persistentVolumeClaim:
          claimName: images-pvc
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you test this in a namespace with multiple image formats and large lists?
- What changes would you make to handle authentication failures and rate-limiting?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
This checks secure defaults and practical CKAD patterns: ConfigMap/Secret usage, correct SecurityContext, and health checks.

## Key Concepts
- SecurityContext: runAsNonRoot, runAsUser, readOnlyRootFilesystem, capabilities: drop: ALL
- ConfigMap and Secret mounting into containers
- Resource requests/limits
- Liveness and readiness probes
- ClusterIP service exposure

## Code Example
```yaml
# Minimal Deployment skeleton (yaml)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: flask-app
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: flask-app
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: flask-app
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: flask
        image: python:3.11-slim
        command: ["python", "/app/main.py"]
        volumeMounts:
        - name: app-config
          mountPath: /app/config
        - name: api-key
          mountPath: /secrets
          readOnly: true
        securityContext:
          runAsUser: 1001
          runAsNonRoot: true
          readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
          allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
          capabilities:
            drop: ["ALL"]
        readinessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /healthz
            port: 5000
          initialDelaySeconds: 5
          periodSeconds: 10
        livenessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /healthz
            port: 5000
          initialDelaySeconds: 15
          periodSeconds: 20
        resources:
          requests:
            cpu: "100m"
            memory: "128Mi"
          limits:
            cpu: "200m"
            memory: "256Mi"
      volumes:
      - name: app-config
        configMap:
          name: flask-config
      - name: api-key
        secret:
          secretName: flask-api-key
```

```yaml
# Minimal Service skeleton
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: flask-service
spec:
  selector:
    app: flask-app
  ports:
  - port: 80
    targetPort: 5000
  type: ClusterIP
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you rotate the API_KEY secret without downtime?
- What are the trade-offs of using readOnlyRootFilesystem in production?
